name: modelmaker
description: Visual pipeline builder for financial model development: the Model-Maker canvas inside VS Code, with GitHub Copilot as its AI.

commands.title: Set Up AI Agent Tools (Cursor, Windsurf)

enumDescriptions: The extension's own Python environment, with Model-Maker shipped in the extension. Made once from any Python 3.11+; holds only Model-Maker's open-source requirements.
The interpreter you selected, with Model-Maker shipped in the extension. Missing requirements are offered for install into it.
The interpreter you selected, with the quantology-modelmaker package installed in it (e.g. pip install -e of a checkout, to develop Model-Maker).
modelmaker.python.environment.markdownDescription: Which Python runs Model-Maker. The first two never install a Model-Maker package: it ships inside the extension, and only its open-source requirements (polars, scikit-learn, …) are installed, from the package index pip is configured for (PyPI or your company mirror).

modelmaker.basePython.markdownDescription: The Python (3.11 or newer) the managed environment is made from. Empty: `modelmaker.pythonPath`, then `py -3` (Windows), `python3` or `python` on PATH.

modelmaker.pythonPath.markdownDescription: The interpreter for the `interpreter` and `installedPackage` environments. Empty uses the Python extension's selection.

modelmaker.autoInstall.markdownDescription: Whether to `pip install` what's missing into a selected interpreter: Model-Maker's requirements (`interpreter` environment) or the package itself (`installedPackage`). The managed environment always installs its requirements.

modelmaker.packageSpec.markdownDescription: For the `installedPackage` environment: what `pip install -U` installs. A PyPI requirement (e.g. `quantology-modelmaker[anthropic]`), or a local path for development (e.g. `-e /path/to/Model-Maker`).

modelmaker.llm.useCopilot.markdownDescription: Offer your GitHub Copilot models to Model-Maker's AI features (drafting blocks, AI builds) and make Copilot the default provider. Other providers stay available in the canvas's Settings.

modelmaker.backend.extraEnv.markdownDescription: Extra environment variables for the backend process, e.g. `{"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "…"}`.

modelmaker.mcp.discovery.markdownDescription: Let `modelmaker-mcp` (Claude Code and other MCP clients) find the open canvases: writes each one's local backend address and access token to `~/.modelmaker/vscode-backends/`, readable by you only, and removes it when the canvas closes.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_open_project
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Opens a Model-Maker project's canvas, so the other modelmaker tools work on it; with create: true, first makes a new, empty project in that folder (model.json, a files/ folder and a git repository). Returns the project's graph. Use this when no canvas is open, or to start a new model from scratch.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Open or create a Model-Maker project

folder.description: The project folder, relative to the workspace folder (e.g. models/pd_2026) or absolute.

create.description: Create the project if the folder has none.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_get_graph
languageModelTools.modelDescription: The open Model-Maker project's pipeline: lanes, every block in run order (id, name, category, lane, status grey/green/orange/red/running, params, input and output ports as name:type, the error of a red block, why an orange block is stale) and every wire. Call this first, and again after edits. Building a model from scratch: add lanes for its phases, a data source block (tag data_sources), tag the target column, then add, wire and run blocks one phase at a time, checking with modelmaker_check as you go.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the open canvas's blocks, wires and statuses

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_list_files
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists a folder on the machine the backend runs on, to find data files for a read_csv/read_parquet/read_excel/read_json block's path param (use the path exactly as returned). Without a path: the project's folder. Also lists the workspace's datasets and sources when it offers them (for read_dataset/read_source blocks).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find data files for the pipeline

path.description: A folder path from an earlier listing.

ext.description: Only files with this extension, e.g. .csv.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_list_block_types
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Without a tag: the block tags (data_sources and exports first, then e.g. data_prep, sampling, binning_woe, regression, performance, stability) with a description of each. With a tag: that tag's blocks (category id and one-sentence summary), built-ins and the user's library. Use describe_block_type before adding one. If no block does what's needed, write one for the library: modelmaker_get_block_guide.

tag.description: A tag from the tag list.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_describe_block_type
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Full documentation for one block category: what it does, its parameters (types, defaults, which ones auto-fill from a column role) and its input/output ports.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_get_output_summary
languageModelTools.modelDescription: A block's last output on one port (default: its first). For a dataframe: row count and each column's dtype, role, nulls, distinct count and mean/std/min/max -- never the rows. For a statistics table (binning summary, metric tables): its rows. For a metric or model: the value. The block must have run (green or orange).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Summarize a block's output (schema and statistics, not rows)

block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

port.description: An output port name; default the first.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_get_input_columns
languageModelTools.modelDescription: The columns (name, dtype, role) a block receives on each input port, from what its upstream blocks last produced -- use it to pick column-valued params such as target, features or by. Empty until the upstream blocks have run.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the columns a block receives

block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_check
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reviews the pipeline as the AI builder would: holdout leakage in the wiring (a binning, WoE or model fitted on rows that include the test/out-of-time sample it is applied to), features fit_binning banded 'suspicious' (IV >= 0.5, usually leakage), and decision hints -- what each green block's result means and what to do next (event counts, IV screens, Gini, PSI, calibration...). With a block: just that block's hints. Report problems to the user rather than silently working around them.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Check the pipeline for leakage and read the hints

block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_get_block_guide
languageModelTools.modelDescription: How to write a new block (or change one) for the user's block library, when no built-in block does what's needed: the library folder to write the .py file into, the files already there, the rules (including how to handle data too big for memory: lazy scans, reduce early, streaming collect) and the commented template. Call this before writing or editing a block file, then modelmaker_check_block_file.
languageModelTools.userDescription: How to write a block for your library

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_check_block_file
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks a block file written in the library folder: re-reads the folder, validates the file (the BLOCKS entry, the functions, the params) and runs its _example_ self-checks. Fix what it reports until ok, then place the block with modelmaker_add_block (its id as the category).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Validate a library block file and run its examples

name.description: The file's name in the library folder, e.g. fannie_mae.py.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_add_lane
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds a lane: a labelled horizontal band that groups one phase of the model (e.g. Data, Sampling, Binning, Estimation, Validation), below the existing ones. Returns its id. Adding a lane whose name exists returns that lane.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a lane to the canvas

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_add_block
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds a block to the canvas, placed in its lane after what's there (it starts grey; wire its inputs with modelmaker_connect, then run it). Params are checked against the block's own. Returns the new block with its id and ports.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a block to the canvas

category.description: The block category (from list/describe block types).

lane.description: Lane id or name to put it in.

params.description: Parameter values; omitted ones take their defaults.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_set_params
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Changes some of a block's parameters (merged into its current ones), and/or renames it or moves it to another lane. Downstream blocks go stale until re-run.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Change a block's parameters, name or lane

block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

params.description: The parameters to change, with their new values.

lane.description: Lane id or name to move it to.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_set_column_role
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Tags a column's role on a block's output, from there downstream: target, id, weight, feature, date, segment, excluded (never to be used as a feature), or unassigned to clear it. Params named target/target_col etc. auto-fill from the roles, so tag the target on the data source block early.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Tag a column's role (target, id, excluded...)

block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_connect
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Wires one block's output port to another block's input port (ports as listed by modelmaker_get_graph, without the :type suffix).

from_block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

to_block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_disconnect
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Removes a wire: give its id (from modelmaker_get_graph), or the input it feeds (to_block and to_port).

to_block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_delete_block
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Deletes a block and the wires to and from it.

block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_run
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs a block and the blocks upstream of it, or with no block the whole pipeline (which also reads the data sources -- a single block's run doesn't), and waits for it. Returns status counts and each affected block's status, with the error of any red block. Also reports any holdout leakage or suspicious features in the pipeline, and the target block's decision hints.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run the pipeline, or up to one block

block.description: A block id (or exact name) from modelmaker_get_graph.

languageModelTools.name: modelmaker_compile
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compiles the pipeline into one self-contained, readable Python script and returns its source. Every block must be green.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Compile the pipeline to a Python script

streaming.description: Fuse compatible stretches into streaming polars queries.

scripts.test: npm run build && node esbuild.mjs --tests && vscode-test
